name: Elgin Mount Pandim
summary: A heritage hotel on the ridge just below Pemayangtse Monastery, a short drive from Upper Pelling. It is the quietest Comfort choice in West Sikkim, with Kangchenjunga views from the lawns.
body: Mount Pandim began as a Sikkim government guest house and is now run by the Elgin group, which also runs heritage hotels in Darjeeling and Kalimpong. It sits on its own wooded spur next to Pemayangtse, so you can walk to the monastery for the morning prayers and to the ruins of Rabdentse without a car.

Rooms are traditional rather than flashy: wooden floors, heaters, and a fixed menu in the dining room. Ask for a room facing the range. The hotel is away from the shops of Upper Pelling, which is the point: evenings are quiet and the night sky is dark.
why: Walking distance to Pemayangtse Monastery and the Rabdentse ruins
Kangchenjunga views from the lawn without the noise of Upper Pelling
Meals included in most plans, which suits a quiet two-night stay
An established operator with heritage hotels across the hills

faqs.q: Is Elgin Mount Pandim in Pelling town
faqs.a: Not quite. It sits about 2 km below Upper Pelling on the spur beside Pemayangtse Monastery, at roughly 2,100 m. The shops and restaurants of Upper Pelling are a 10-minute drive or a 30-minute uphill walk. Most guests like the distance, because the hotel is quiet at night and the monastery is a five-minute walk away for the early prayers.

faqs.q: Can you see Kangchenjunga from the rooms
faqs.a: On a clear morning, yes, from the lawns and from the rooms on the valley side. Views are best from October to early December and again in March and April. In the monsoon, from June to September, cloud usually hides the range for days at a time. Ask for a mountain-facing room when you book, and check the latest room plan with the hotel.

faqs.q: Is it worth the price over a Value hotel in Upper Pelling
faqs.a: If you want a quiet stay with history around you and meals included, yes. If you mainly want to sleep and spend your days out sightseeing, a good Value hotel in Upper Pelling at ₹3,000–5,000 a night gives similar mountain views for less. We suggest Mount Pandim for couples and slower trips of two nights or more.

name: The Norbu Ghang Resort
summary: A long-running resort in Upper Pelling with terraced cottages facing the Kangchenjunga range. It is our usual Value pick when families want space and a view without paying heritage-hotel rates.
body: Norbu Ghang is one of the older established properties in Pelling, built in stepped blocks down the hillside so that most rooms look across the Rathong valley to the snow peaks. It is a short walk from the Upper Pelling helipad ground and the main row of restaurants.

Rooms are plain and warm, with heaters in winter. Service is steady rather than polished. Prices swing with the season: October, the Puja holidays and late December are the most expensive, while the monsoon brings large discounts.
why: Most rooms face the range, which is why you come to Pelling
Walkable to Upper Pelling restaurants and the helipad viewpoint
Family rooms and cottages for groups of three or four
Good monsoon and winter discounts

faqs.q: Where is Norbu Ghang in Pelling
faqs.a: It is in Upper Pelling, the higher of Pelling's two clusters, at around 2,100 m. The helipad ground, which is the best free viewpoint in town, and most restaurants are within a 5 to 10-minute walk. Cars can drive to the reception. Pemayangtse Monastery is about 3 km away by road.

faqs.q: Does it suit families with small children
faqs.a: Yes, with a caution. The cottages are on terraces linked by steps, so a pram is no use and toddlers need watching on the stairways. Family rooms sleep three or four. The restaurant serves simple Indian, Chinese and Sikkimese food, which children usually eat without fuss. Ask for a lower block if anyone in your group finds steps hard.

From mid-June to mid-September, during the monsoon, rates usually drop well below the rack price, and January and February can also be cheaper. October, the Durga Puja and Diwali holidays, and Christmas to New Year are the most expensive and sell out first. Prices are indicative, so confirm the current rate directly or through us before you travel.

name: Upper Pelling family guesthouses
summary: Small family-run guesthouses and lodges line the lanes of Upper Pelling, many with rooftop views of Kangchenjunga. They are the cheapest way to stay in Pelling without giving up the view.
body: Upper Pelling has dozens of small lodges of three to ten rooms, usually run by the family that lives on the ground floor. Rooms are basic: a double bed, thick blankets, an attached bathroom with a geyser that may only run at set hours. Many have a flat roof where you can watch the sunrise on the range.

We pick these places on recent experience rather than by name, because standards change with each season. Ask for a room on the top floor, check that hot water works, and agree the price, including any heater charge, before you carry your bags up.
why: The same mountain view as hotels costing three times as much
Home-cooked dal-bhat, momos and thukpa from the family kitchen
Easy to change plans, as most take walk-in guests outside peak weeks
Money goes straight to local families

faqs.q: Do I need to book a Pelling guesthouse in advance
faqs.a: In October, during the Puja holidays and from Christmas to New Year, yes, book a few days ahead because rooms fill with groups from Kolkata. The rest of the year you can usually find a room by walking around Upper Pelling in the afternoon. Arrive before dark, compare two or three places, and look at the room before paying.

faqs.q: Is there heating in budget rooms
faqs.a: Most budget rooms have no built-in heating. Owners lend an electric heater for about ₹200–300 a night in winter, and give thick quilts. From December to February nights at 2,100 m fall to around 2–5°C, so bring warm sleepwear. Power cuts happen, so a head torch is useful.

Yes. Almost every owner can book a local car for the Pelling sightseeing loop, a seat on the morning shared jeep to Yuksom or Siliguri, or a reserved car to Gangtok. Their prices are close to the local taxi union rates. Ask the night before, because shared jeeps leave early and seats are limited.

name: Yuksom village homestays
price_band: ₹1,500–3,000 per person per night with meals
summary: Family homestays in Yuksom, run mainly by Bhutia, Limbu and Nepali households, are the natural base before or after the Goecha La and Dzongri treks. Meals are home-cooked and hosts know the trail well.
body: Yuksom is a small village at 1,780 m, and much of its accommodation is in family homes and small lodges around the central lanes and towards Dubdi Monastery. Rooms are simple and clean, often wood-panelled, with shared or attached bathrooms. Dinner is usually rice, dal, a local green such as nettle or fern shoots, and a meat or egg dish.

Hosts are often connected to trekking guides, porters and yak or pony owners, which makes them useful when arranging a trek or a day walk. We do not name individual homes here because they change hands and standards; we pick them each season on recent stays.
why: Meals included, so the daily cost is easy to predict
Hosts who can connect you with registered trekking guides
A quiet, walkable village with three historic sites within 3 km
Your money stays in the village

faqs.q: Can I leave luggage at a Yuksom homestay during a trek
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Most homestays will store a bag safely while you trek to Dzongri or Goecha La, often free if you stay with them before and after. Lock it, label it with your name and dates, and keep passports and permits with you on the trek. Confirm the arrangement when you book.

faqs.q: What do Yuksom homestays serve for food
faqs.a: Expect home food: rice, dal, a vegetable such as squash or local greens, pickle, and often chicken or egg. Breakfast is usually bread, eggs, or puri and potato curry. Some hosts make churpi soup or sel roti on request. Vegetarian meals are easy to arrange. Bottled water is sold in the village, but most homes give boiled water if you ask.

faqs.q: Is there mobile signal in Yuksom
faqs.a: Yes, in the village. BSNL, Jio and Airtel usually work in Yuksom, with 4G that slows in the evening and in bad weather. Signal fades soon after you leave on the Goecha La trail and is patchy at Tshoka and Dzongri, so tell family your plan before you start. Some homestays have Wi-Fi, but do not count on it.

name: Yangsum Heritage Farm
price_band: ₹4,000–6,500 per room per night with meals
summary: A working family farm below Rinchenpong, with rooms in an old farmhouse dating from the 1820s and a newer cottage. It is one of the best-known farmstays in Sikkim and a calm alternative to Pelling hotels.
body: Yangsum is the home farm of a long-established Rinchenpong family. Guests stay in the restored farmhouse or a cottage, eat meals made from the farm's own cardamom, vegetables, rice and dairy, and walk out through orange orchards and terraced fields. The view across the valley takes in the Kangchenjunga range on clear days.

It suits travellers who want to slow down for two nights, read, walk to Rinchenpong Monastery and the old village paths, and talk to their hosts about farming in West Sikkim. It is not a hotel, so expect simple rooms and fixed meal times.
why: Food grown on the farm and cooked in the family kitchen
A real working farm with orchards and cardamom groves
Easy walks to Rinchenpong Monastery and the old poison lake
Quiet nights, far from tourist traffic

faqs.q: How do I reach Yangsum Heritage Farm
faqs.a: It is just below Rinchenpong village in West Sikkim, about 40 km and 1.5–2 hours from Pelling or about 130 km and 5 hours from Siliguri via Jorethang. The last stretch is a narrow village road, so confirm directions with the farm. Shared jeeps run from Jorethang to Rinchenpong, from where the farm can arrange a pick-up.

Most plans include all meals, served at set times. Food is mostly vegetarian Sikkimese and Nepali home cooking using produce from the farm, with meat on request. Tell the hosts about allergies or dietary needs in advance, because the nearest shops are in Rinchenpong and Kaluk. Rates are indicative; confirm the current meal plan when you book.

Older children who like animals, orchards and walking usually enjoy it. There is no television, swimming pool or play area, and paths are uneven and steep in places, so it is less suited to toddlers. Families who want to see how a hill farm works, from cardamom drying to milking, find it one of the most rewarding stays in Sikkim.

name: Mt Narsing Village Resort
summary: A small resort of wooden cottages in a garden outside Ravangla, one of the older tourist stays in South Sikkim. It is a good base for Buddha Park, Ralang Monastery and the Maenam trek.
body: The resort is a cluster of cottages set among trees on the edge of Ravangla, away from the main bazaar. Cottages are built in a local style with wooden interiors and small sit-outs. On clear mornings the Kangchenjunga range shows over the ridges to the north-west.

Ravangla is cold for most of the year, so heaters and hot water matter here more than décor. Mt Narsing keeps things simple and warm, and staff can arrange cars to Buddha Park, Ralang, Temi Tea Garden and Namchi.
why: Cottages with space and quiet, away from the market
Short drive to Buddha Park and Ralang Monastery
Staff who arrange guides for the Maenam Hill walk
Fair prices outside the Pang Lhabsol and Puja weeks

faqs.q: How far is Mt Narsing Village Resort from Buddha Park
faqs.a: Buddha Park (Tathagata Tsal) is a few kilometres away, about 10–15 minutes by car. Ralang Monastery is around 30 minutes' drive, and Temi Tea Garden roughly an hour. The Ravangla bazaar, with shared jeep stands for Gangtok, Namchi and Pelling, is a short drive. Distances are approximate, so confirm with the resort.

Yes. At over 2,000 m Ravangla is often misty and cool even in summer, with nights around 10–15°C. From December to February nights drop close to freezing. Ask for a heater, carry a warm jacket and a hat, and expect damp, foggy days in the monsoon from June to September.

faqs.q: Should I stay in Ravangla or Namchi
faqs.a: Stay in Ravangla if you want cooler air, the Buddha Park at dawn and a walk to Maenam or Ralang. Stay in Namchi if you want a larger town with more hotels and restaurants, closer to Samdruptse and Char Dham. They are about 25 km and an hour apart, so one night in either place covers both.
